stem: Where is the duct opening for the parotid gland located in the mouth?

options.text: Under the tongue near the midline
On the hard palate near the rugae
On the buccal mucosa opposite the second molar (tooth 6)
At the base of the anterior pillar of the fauces

explanation: The parotid duct, which secretes serous saliva, opens on the cheek opposite the upper first molar.
rationale: This gland is located in the cheek area.

optionExplanations.A: This is the location for the submandibular and sublingual salivary gland ducts.
optionExplanations.B: The hard palate contains minor salivary glands, but not the primary parotid duct.
optionExplanations.C: The parotid duct, which secretes serous saliva, opens on the cheek opposite the upper first molar.
optionExplanations.D: This area is associated with tonsillar tissue rather than the parotid duct opening.

source.hint: This gland is located in the cheek area.
